name: Intel Corporation

segments.note: Segment revenue includes Intel Foundry's $17.7B of sales to Intel's own product groups, which are eliminated in the total. Corporate unallocated costs of $5.5B ($11.2B in 2024) are not in any segment.

sections.title: Quarterly revenue
sections.callout: Outlook: Intel guided Q1 2026 revenue to $11.7B–$12.7B, with a GAAP loss of $0.21 per share.

footnotes: Net loss is attributable to Intel, after $300M to noncontrolling interests; the company as a whole earned $30M. Altera was deconsolidated on Sep 12, 2025.
Free cash flow = operating cash flow − additions to property, plant & equipment (calculated; Intel's own adjusted measure differs). Total liabilities = total liabilities and equity − total equity.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Intel's revenue was flat at $52.9B in 2025 (down 0.5%). Client Computing fell 3.4% to $32.2B while Data Center and AI grew 4.9% to $16.9B. The operating loss shrank to $2.2B from $11.7B as R&D and restructuring costs fell.

Net loss attributable to Intel narrowed to $300M ($0.06 per share) from $18.8B, helped by $3.8B of investment gains, interest and other income. Capital spending fell 38.8% to $14.6B, and cash and short-term investments rose to $37.4B.
highlights: Data Center and AI operating income more than doubled to $3.4B.
Intel Foundry's operating loss narrowed to $10.3B from $13.3B.
watch: Intel Foundry still lost $10.3B, on revenue mostly from Intel itself.
Free cash flow remained negative at about −$4.9B.
Diluted share count rose 5.8% as Intel issued new shares.
Q1 2026 guidance calls for a GAAP loss of $0.21 per share.
